title: Ajanta Caves
summary: The Ajanta Caves are thirty rock-cut Buddhist caves, counting unfinished ones, cut into a cliff above the Waghora river in Maharashtra, India. Five are sanctuaries (chaityagrihas) and the rest monasteries. Excavation came in two phases about four centuries apart, in the 2nd to 1st centuries BCE and the 5th to 6th centuries CE; the later phase added mural paintings and sculpture.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO gives 'about the 2nd century BCE' to the 1st century BCE for the first phase and the 5th to 6th centuries CE for the second, with no finer dates. Start -199 is the first year of the 2nd century BCE and end 600 the last year of the 6th century CE; the true span of excavation is shorter. Two phases with a gap of about four centuries lie between.

as_recorded.value: The first phase coincides with the rule of the Satavahana dynasty from about the 2nd century BCE to the 1st century BCE, while the second phase corresponds to the Basim branch of the Vakataka dynasty with their Asmaka and Rishika feudatories in the 5th to 6th centuries CE.
A first group of caves was created in the second century B.C.
A second group of caves was created at a later date, the fifth and sixth centuries A.D.

when.display: Excavated in two phases: 2nd–1st centuries BCE and 5th–6th centuries CE

where.modern_name: Ajanta Caves, Soegaon taluka, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) district, Maharashtra, India
where.historical_name: The Ajanta cave monasteries and sanctuaries above the left bank of the river Waghora, in the Satavahana period (first phase) and the Vakataka period (second phase)

importance.justification: UNESCO says Ajanta exemplifies one of the greatest achievements in ancient Buddhist rock-cut architecture; ICOMOS rates its mural paintings among the major achievements of Gupta and post-Gupta style.

sources.title: Advisory Body Evaluation (ICOMOS): Ajanta Caves, no. 242
sources.author: ICOMOS

reviewer_note: No model: Ajanta is a complex of thirty caves; no page opened gives a height and plan for one structure. The UNESCO point (20°33'11.2" N, 75°42'0.9" E, converted to decimal) is within about 0.1 km of the OSM point. Least sure of the date span, which is the outer limit of two excavation phases rather than a construction date; the ICOMOS French text says 5th to 7th centuries where its English text says 5th and 6th.
